title: UK restaurants turn back to the phone as AI booking assistants arrive, the Guardian reports
summary: The Guardian reports UK restaurant owners returning to phone bookings as assistants like Meta's Muse launch there, and Resy banning bots. Meta says Muse makes lives easier; a mid-November report said Muse's calling worked only for US businesses, so the bot that called Bouchon Racine is unnamed.

topics.angle: What AI agents do to the businesses on the other end.

claims.text: Restaurant owners in the UK are returning to the telephone instead of online booking as AI assistants such as Meta's Muse launch there, the Guardian reports.
Resy has banned bots after restaurants on its platform were swarmed by agents that refresh pages thousands of times and take all the reservations, the Guardian reports.
Dave Strauss, co-owner of Bouchon Racine, told the Guardian an AI bot phoned to book, said it was an AI booking process when asked, and that he told it never to call again.
Jeremy King, who owns Simpson's in the Strand, said he is going more analogue, and diners will find it easier to get a prime table by phone.
Meta says Muse can make people's lives easier, and it has deals with British businesses including Marks & Spencer, Currys, Sainsbury's and easyJet; Meta had not commented to the Guardian.
As of 13 November, Muse's calling feature worked only for paying users calling US businesses, and not for anyone in the UK, Gadget reported.
Which assistant made the call to Bouchon Racine is not named in the report.

to_find: Resy's own statement on banning bots
would_change: Meta naming the bot, or Muse calling coming to the UK.
